heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In the operating cell Mg ∣ Mg<sup>2+</sup> ∣∣ Ag<sup>+</sup> ∣ Ag, electrons travel through the wire in which direction?
solution: C - Mg to Ag Mg is oxidised to Mg<sup>2+</sup> at the anode. Ag<sup>+</sup> is reduced to Ag at the cathode, so electrons travel through the wire from Mg to Ag.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a working Zn–Cu cell with a KNO<sub>3</sub> bridge, which ion migrates towards the zinc compartment?
solution: A - NO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup> Zn<sup>2+</sup> accumulates at the anode as Zn oxidises. Nitrate ions enter that compartment to offset the buildup of positive charge.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: E°(Fe<sup>2+</sup>/Fe) = −0.44 V and E°(Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu) = +0.34 V. What is E° for spontaneous iron oxidation by Cu<sup>2+</sup>?
solution: D - 0.78 V Cu<sup>2+</sup> is reduced and Fe is oxidised. Using reduction potentials, E° = +0.34 − (−0.44) = +0.78 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which metal can reduce Zn<sup>2+</sup> under standard conditions? E°(Zn<sup>2+</sup>/Zn) = −0.76 V.
solution: D - Mg, E° = −2.37 V Mg has the more negative reduction potential. Pairing Mg oxidation with Zn<sup>2+</sup> reduction gives E° = −0.76 − (−2.37) = +1.61 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In Zn + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Zn<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, how does increasing [Cu<sup>2+</sup>] alone affect the EMF at fixed temperature?
options: Makes it zero at any concentration
solution: B - Increases it Q = a(Zn<sup>2+</sup>)/a(Cu<sup>2+</sup>). Increasing Cu<sup>2+</sup> lowers Q, so the subtraction term in E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q becomes smaller and E increases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For a two-electron reaction at 298 K, E° = 0.40 V and Q = 10<sup>2</sup>. Use 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V. What is E?

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A cell has E° = 0.118 V at 298 K and n = 1. Using 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, find K.
solution: C - 10<sup>2</sup> At equilibrium E = 0 and Q = K, so log K = nE°/0.059 = 0.118/0.059 = 2. Thus K = 100.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: For n = 2 and E° = 0.80 V, find ΔG° using F = 96 500 C mol<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which statements hold when a reversible cell reaction reaches equilibrium?
options: Q = K and E = E° always
solution: A - Q = K and E = 0 At equilibrium the reaction quotient has reached K and ΔG = 0. The relation ΔG = −nFE then gives E = 0.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Why is the pure metal absent from the Nernst reaction quotient in a typical metal–metal-ion cell?
options: Activity of dissolved ions, taken as 1
Activity of a pure solid, taken as 1
solution: C - Activity of a pure solid, taken as 1 A pure solid has unit activity. Including that factor in the quotient would simply multiply or divide by one.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: The resistance of an electrolyte in the same conductivity cell rises fourfold. What happens to conductivity?
solution: B - Falls to one-fourth Conductivity equals the cell constant divided by resistance. With fixed geometry, a fourfold resistance gives one-fourth the conductivity.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A cell with constant 0.80 cm<sup>-1</sup> contains a solution of conductance 0.020 S. Find κ.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: κ = 0.0015 S cm<sup>-1</sup> at 0.010 M. Find Λm.
solution: C - 150 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> Λm = 1000κ/c = 1000 × 0.0015/0.010 = 150 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup> when c is in mol L<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which geometrical change doubles the cell constant ℓ/A?
solution: A - Doubling electrode separation alone The cell constant is ℓ/A. Doubling ℓ at fixed A doubles ℓ/A.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which pair of trends usually occurs on diluting an electrolyte?
solution: A - κ decreases and Λm increases Dilution usually lowers the number of ions per unit volume and hence κ. Interionic interactions decrease and weak electrolytes ionise more, so Λm increases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which plot can be extrapolated approximately linearly to determine Λ°m for a strong electrolyte at low concentration?
solution: B - Λm versus √c At low concentration a strong electrolyte follows Λm ≈ Λ°m − A√c. The intercept of Λm against √c is Λ°m.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which combination gives Λ°m(CH<sub>3</sub>COOH)?
solution: D - Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH<sub>3</sub>COONa) − Λ°m(NaCl) Kohlrausch’s law allows ionic sums. Add HCl and CH<sub>3</sub>COONa, then subtract NaCl to cancel Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> and retain H<sup>+</sup> and acetate.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A weak electrolyte has Λm = 12 and Λ°m = 300 S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>. Estimate its degree of dissociation.
solution: C - 0.040 The weak-electrolyte estimate is α = Λm/Λ°m = 12/300 = 0.040, or 4.0%.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How much charge is needed to discharge 0.25 mol of Al<sup>3+</sup> completely?
solution: D - 0.75 F Al<sup>3+</sup> + 3e<sup>-</sup> → Al. The charge for 0.25 mol is 3 × 0.25 = 0.75 faraday, or approximately 72 375 C.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: A 2.00 A current passes for 965 s. How many moles of electrons pass? F = 96 500 C mol<sup>-1</sup>.
solution: B - 0.0200 mol Q = It = 2.00 × 965 = 1930 C. The amount of electrons is 1930/96 500 = 0.0200 mol.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: How much Ag is deposited by 0.10 F from AgNO<sub>3</sub> at 100% efficiency? M(Ag) = 108 g mol<sup>-1</sup>.
solution: B - 10.8 g Ag<sup>+</sup> needs one electron per ion, so 0.10 F deposits 0.10 mol of Ag. The mass is 0.10 × 108 = 10.8 g.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: The same charge deposits Cu from Cu<sup>2+</sup> and Ag from Ag<sup>+</sup>. What is the mole ratio Ag : Cu?
solution: D - 2 : 1 Ag<sup>+</sup> requires one electron per ion and Cu<sup>2+</sup> requires two. Equal charge deposits twice as many moles of Ag as Cu.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which species forms at the anode during electrolysis of molten NaCl?
solution: B - Cl<sub>2</sub> At the anode chloride is oxidised: 2Cl<sup>-</sup> → Cl<sub>2</sub> + 2e<sup>-</sup>. Sodium ions are reduced at the cathode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which gas is released at the cathode during electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes?
solution: A - H<sub>2</sub> In aqueous brine, water is reduced at the cathode: 2H<sub>2</sub>O + 2e<sup>-</sup> → H<sub>2</sub> + 2OH<sup>-</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which solid accumulates at both plates of a lead storage battery during discharge?
solution: D - PbSO<sub>4</sub> Pb at the negative plate and PbO<sub>2</sub> at the positive plate both become PbSO<sub>4</sub> during discharge, consuming sulfuric acid.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: What happens to sulfuric acid concentration during charging of a lead storage battery?
solution: B - It rises. Charging reverses the discharge reaction. PbSO<sub>4</sub> is converted back into the active plate materials and sulfuric acid is regenerated.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Which cell is designed for repeated charging and discharging?
solution: C - Lead storage battery The lead storage battery is a secondary cell. Applying an external current reverses its discharge reaction so it can be used repeatedly.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, which reactant is supplied to the electrode at which oxidation occurs?
solution: D - H<sub>2</sub> at the anode Hydrogen is the fuel and loses electrons at the anode. Oxygen accepts electrons at the cathode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: In aerated neutral water, what is the usual cathodic product when O<sub>2</sub> is reduced during iron corrosion?
solution: A - OH<sup>-</sup> The neutral-water cathodic half-reaction is O<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O + 4e<sup>-</sup> → 4OH<sup>-</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Connecting Mg to iron suppresses rusting because Mg does what?
options: Acts as a passive layer of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>
Increases the rate of iron oxidation
solution: C - Oxidises preferentially Mg oxidises preferentially to Mg<sup>2+</sup>. It supplies electrons to the iron, acting as a sacrificial anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each cell symbol with its meaning.
Column I
Column II
P. Single vertical line
1. Inert conducting electrode
Q. Double vertical line
2. Phase boundary
R. Pt(s) beside H2
3. Salt bridge or liquid junction
S. Cell notation from left to right
4. Anode to cathode for the stated galvanic reaction
solution: D - P–2, Q–3, R–1, S–4 A single line shows a phase boundary, a double line a liquid junction, Pt is an inert conductor, and conventional galvanic notation places the anode first.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each numerical condition with E for a cell having E° = 0.50 V, n = 2 at 298 K. Use
2.303RT/F = 0.059 V.
Column I
Column II
P. Q = 1
1. 0.559 V
Q. Q = 102
2. 0.441 V
R. Q = 10-2
3. 0.382 V
S. Q = 104
4. 0.500 V
solution: D - P–4, Q–2, R–1, S–3 Substitute in E = 0.50 − (0.059/2)log Q. For the four Q values the potentials are 0.500, 0.441, 0.559 and 0.382 V.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each quantity with its relation.
Column I
Column II
P. Conductance G
1. ℓ/A
Q. Conductivity κ
2. 1/R
R. Cell constant
3. 1000κ/c for c in mol L-1
S. Molar conductivity in S cm2 mol-1
4. G × cell constant
solution: B - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 G = 1/R, κ = Gℓ/A, cell constant = ℓ/A, and Λm = 1000κ/c for c in mol L<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each quantity with a valid unit.
Column I
Column II
P. Conductivity
1. Ω
Q. Molar conductivity
2. S cm-1
R. Resistance
3. cm-1
S. Cell constant
4. S cm2 mol-1
solution: A - P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3 Conductivity is in S cm<sup>-1</sup>, molar conductivity in S cm<sup>2</sup> mol<sup>-1</sup>, resistance in Ω, and ℓ/A in cm<sup>-1</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each ion with charge needed to deposit 1 mol of the metal.
Column I
Column II
P. Ag+
1. 4F
Q. Cu2+
2. F
R. Al3+
3. 3F
S. Sn4+
4. 2F
solution: C - P–2, Q–4, R–3, S–1 One mole of metal receives the number of electron moles given by the ionic charge: 1 for Ag<sup>+</sup>, 2 for Cu<sup>2+</sup>, 3 for Al<sup>3+</sup> and 4 for Sn<sup>4+</sup>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each electrode process with its product.
Column I
Column II
P. Cathode of molten NaCl electrolysis
1. Cl2
Q. Anode of molten NaCl electrolysis
2. O2
R. Cathode of brine electrolysis
3. Na
S. Inert anode during electrolysis of acidified water
4. H2
solution: A - P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2 Molten NaCl gives Na at the cathode and Cl<sub>2</sub> at the anode. Aqueous brine gives H<sub>2</sub> at the cathode, and acidified water gives O<sub>2</sub> at the inert anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each electrochemical device with its identifying feature.
Column I
Column II
P. Lead storage battery
1. Pb and PbO2 plates
Q. Leclanché dry cell
2. HgO cathode active material
R. Mercury cell
3. Zinc container and MnO2 depolariser
S. Hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell
4. Continuous supply of reactant gases
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 The lead battery has Pb/PbO<sub>2</sub> plates. The Leclanché cell uses zinc and MnO<sub>2</sub>, the mercury cell uses HgO, and a fuel cell uses externally supplied gases.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each fuel-cell or corrosion process to its equation.
Column I
Column II
P. H2 oxidation in alkaline medium
1. H2 + 2OH- → 2H2O + 2e-
Q. O2 reduction in alkaline medium
2. Fe2+ + 2OH- → Fe(OH)2
R. Anodic dissolution of iron
3. O2 + 2H2O + 4e- → 4OH-
S. Precipitation of ferrous hydroxide
4. Fe → Fe2+ + 2e-
solution: B - P–1, Q–3, R–4, S–2 H<sub>2</sub> loses electrons in alkaline medium, while O<sub>2</sub> gains electrons to give OH<sup>-</sup>. Iron loses electrons to Fe<sup>2+</sup>, which combines with OH<sup>-</sup> to precipitate Fe(OH)<sub>2</sub>.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match the condition with its thermodynamic implication for the reaction as written.
Column I
Column II
P. E° > 0
1. K > 1
Q. E° < 0
2. ΔG° > 0
R. E° = 0=K
3. ΔG < 0 under those conditions
S. E > 0 under actual conditions
4. 1
solution: A - P–1, Q–2, R–4, S–3 E° > 0 gives K > 1, and E° < 0 gives ΔG° > 0. For row R, read “E° = 0” on the left and “K = 1” on the right. E > 0 gives ΔG < 0 under the stated conditions.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question:
Match each conductivity observation with its explanation.
Column I
Column II
P. Λm of weak electrolyte rises steeply on dilution
1. Ionisation increases substantially
Q. Conductivity usually falls on dilution
2. Kohlrausch’s law
R. Limiting ionic contributions add
3. Fewer charge carriers per unit volume
S. Alternating current used in conductivity
measurement
4. Reduced electrode polarisation
solution: C - P–1, Q–3, R–2, S–4 Weak-electrolyte ionisation rises upon dilution. Ions per unit volume fall, ionic contributions add at infinite dilution, and alternating current reduces electrode polarisation.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) E°cell remains unchanged when the balanced reaction is multiplied by two. Reason (R) Cell potential is an extensive property.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Doubling the reaction doubles n and ΔG°, leaving −ΔG°/(nF) unchanged. Potential is intensive.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Zn is the anode in an operating Daniell cell. Reason (R) Zn is oxidised to Zn<sup>2+</sup> in the spontaneous cell reaction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Zn loses electrons to form Zn<sup>2+</sup>, and oxidation defines the anode.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A salt bridge helps maintain electrical neutrality in each half-cell. Reason (R) Electrons travel through the salt bridge from anode to cathode.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Salt-bridge ions move to preserve neutrality. Electrons travel in the external wire.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Depositing one mole of Al requires three faradays from Al<sup>3+</sup>. Reason (R) Each Al<sup>3+</sup> ion gains three electrons.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. One mole of Al<sup>3+</sup> accepts 3 mol of electrons, so deposition requires 3 F.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A fuel cell can keep operating while reactants are supplied. Reason (R) A fuel cell stores all reactants permanently inside its electrodes.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: C - A is true and R is false A is true and R is false. Fuel flows in from outside and the cell operates while reactants are supplied and products can be removed.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A Mg block can protect iron against corrosion. Reason (R) Mg oxidises more readily than iron and acts as a sacrificial anode.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: A - Both A and R are true, and R explains A Both are true. Mg has the more negative reduction potential and oxidises in preference to Fe.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) A standard hydrogen electrode is assigned zero standard potential. Reason (R) Its inert conductor is platinum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The zero potential of the standard hydrogen electrode is assigned by convention. Platinum supplies an inert conducting surface.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Lead storage batteries are secondary cells. Reason (R) The electrolyte in a lead storage battery contains sulfuric acid.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: B - Both A and R are true, and R does not explain A Both are true. The battery is secondary because discharge can be reversed by charging. Sulfuric acid is its electrolyte.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) The EMF at equilibrium is always equal to the standard EMF. Reason (R) The reaction quotient equals K at equilibrium.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. At Q = K the equilibrium EMF is zero, while E° is defined for standard states and need not be zero.

heading: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
title: 12th Ch 2 Electrochemistry Practice MCQ Level 1
question: Assertion (A) Molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte decreases on dilution. Reason (R) Dilution increases the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not correctly explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
solution: D - A is false and R is true A is false and R is true. Dilution increases the degree of dissociation and therefore increases molar conductivity.
